intuition.title: Use the detailed A/B labels and retain the summary conflict
intuition.text: The concluding sentence on p. 345 reverses the with/without-isopropyl-alcohol order relative to the explicit A/B preparation, Figure 1 caption and detailed phase assignments. Preserve sample A = water = hexagonal and sample B = water/isopropyl alcohol = cubic from the detailed sample-linked evidence; retain this conclusion conflict rather than silently correcting the source.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied PDF pp. 1–2, detailed A/B assignments, Figures 1–2 captions and concluding sentence

intuition.title: Crystallite and particle sizes describe different measurements
intuition.text: Sample A has a reported Scherrer crystallite size of 5.3 nm and a TEM particle size of about 8 nm; sample B has 3.5 nm and around 5 nm, respectively. The source initially calls these consistent and later notes the TEM values are slightly larger. No exact equivalence, combined average, confidence interval or numerical distribution width is inferred.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied PDF p. 1, Scherrer paragraph; p. 2, TEM paragraph

intuition.title: Solvent effects and radical pathways are proposed
intuition.text: The authors associate isopropyl alcohol with reduced aggregation and altered CdS phase selection, and propose different radical-mediated routes to sulfide from thiosulfate. The reaction equations and kinetic explanation are source interpretation. No measured radical concentration, intermediate yield or comparative rate constant is supplied.

intuition.title: XPS is a qualitative statement without displayed data

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Prospects of Colloidal Nanocrystals for Electronic and Optoelectronic Applications

general_background.title: Solvent and transport
general_background.summary: A solvent carries dissolved species and transports heat through a reaction or dispersion. Solubility, viscosity and molecular interactions affect how precursors and ligand-coated particles move and mix.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
